items.name: .22 Long Rifle Automatic (Colt Woodsman)
items.notes: Low damage, light recoil sidearm favored for target shooting and discreet carry.

items.name: .32 Revolver (Colt Pocket Positive)
items.notes: Highly dependable pocket revolver with a reliable mechanical cylinder action.

items.name: .38 Automatic (Colt Model 1903)
items.notes: Standard civilian and police self-defense pistol offering balanced stopping power.

items.name: .45 Automatic (Colt M1911)
items.notes: Military-grade heavy semi-automatic sidearm with substantial kinetic stopping power.

items.name: 9mm Automatic (Glock 17)
items.notes: Ubiquitous modern law enforcement sidearm with standard high-capacity polymer magazines.

items.name: .44 Magnum Revolver (Smith & Wesson Model 29)
items.notes: Modern heavy-framed hunting revolver capable of stopping large beasts (or cult entities) dead in their tracks.

items.name: .41 Derringer
items.notes: Tiny, easily concealed two-shot pocket pistol. Fatal at point-blank range, useless at distance.

items.name: Mauser C96 'Broomhandle'
items.notes: Distinctive semi-automatic pistol featuring an integrated box magazine in front of the trigger.

items.name: .45 Smith & Wesson Schofield
items.notes: Top-break revolver popular in the American West; fast manual extraction and reloading cycles.

items.name: .38 Smith & Wesson Safety Hammerless
items.notes: Concealed hammer design nicknamed the 'Lemon Squeezer'. Cannot catch on clothing fabrics during an emergency draw.

items.name: Webley Mark IV Revolver
items.notes: Standard British military service revolver; heavy unjacketed lead round ensures significant stopping power.

items.name: .357 Magnum Revolver (Colt Python)
items.notes: Premium modern double-action revolver recognized for its exceptional match-grade accuracy and frame strength.

items.name: Colt Single Action Army (.45 Colt)
items.notes: The classic 'Peacemaker' six-shooter. Slow to reload using a loading gate, but an icon of the Old West.

items.name: Luger P08 (9mm)
items.notes: Distinctive German toggle-locked semi-automatic pistol. Highly prized collector's item in the modern era.

items.name: Snub-Nose .38 Special (Smith & Wesson)
items.notes: Short-barreled concealable revolver. Easy to hide but suffers from severe accuracy penalties at range.

items.name: Beretta M9 (9mm)
items.notes: Standard issue US military sidearm until recently; reliable double-action semi-automatic.

items.name: Desert Eagle (.50 AE)
items.notes: Massive gas-operated semi-automatic handgun. Extreme recoil and damage, prone to jamming if not gripped firmly.

items.name: .30-06 Bolt Action Rifle (M1903 Springfield)
items.notes: High-powered military/hunting rifle boasting extreme range and accuracy.

items.name: .22 Bolt-Action Hunting Rifle
items.notes: Common farm tool used for vermin control; quiet and easy to acquire without raising suspicion.

items.name: 12-Gauge Shotgun (Pump Action)
items.notes: Devastating at close range; wide pellet spread grants better hit probability against moving targets.

items.name: 12-Gauge Shotgun (Double-Barrel Break Open)
items.notes: Classic defensive firearm found in rural homes. Reliable mechanics allow firing both barrels simultaneously.

items.name: .470 Nitro Express Elephant Gun
items.notes: Massive double-barreled rifle designed for big-game hunting. Inflicts immense damage but suffers severe recoil.

items.name: .30-30 Winchester Lever-Action Rifle
items.notes: The classic American deer rifle; iconic under-lever operation provides a swift secondary shot cycle.

items.name: .303 Lee-Enfield Bolt-Action Rifle
items.notes: Standard British infantry rifle; ruggedly constructed bolt action is highly resistant to battlefield muck and grit.

items.name: 10-Gauge Lever-Action Shotgun (Winchester 1887)
items.notes: Intimidating, heavy-gauge repeating shotgun. Harder to control than a 12-gauge but strikes with brutal kinetic force.

items.name: M4 Carbine Semi-Automatic Rifle
items.notes: Modern civilian-legal tactical rifle; accepts standard 30-round detachable box magazines and optics rails.

items.name: .50 BMG Anti-Materiel Rifle (Barrett M82)
items.notes: Massive semi-automatic precision rifle. Engineered to punch straight through engine blocks, structural walls, and armored monstrosities.

items.name: Martini-Henry (.577/450)
items.notes: British falling-block single-shot rifle. Powerful and rugged, but slow to cycle and generates huge clouds of blackpowder smoke.

items.name: Winchester 1873 (.44-40)
items.notes: 'The Gun that Won the West.' Tubular magazine lever-action rifle, smooth to operate but uses older, less powerful rimmed ammunition.

items.name: AK-47 Assault Rifle (7.62x39mm)
items.notes: Soviet-designed selective-fire assault rifle. Incredibly durable and reliable in muddy, dirty, or blood-soaked conditions.

items.name: Remington 870 (12-Gauge Pump)
items.notes: The ubiquitous modern pump-action shotgun. Used globally by police, military, and civilians for lethal close-quarters stopping power.

items.name: .45 Thompson SMG ('Tommy Gun')
items.notes: Infamous gangland automatic weapon utilizing either 20-round box or 50-round drum magazines.

items.name: 12-Gauge Browning Auto-5 Shotgun
items.notes: Early semi-automatic shotgun variant capable of rapid, cyclic close-quarters defensive fire.

items.name: Gatling Gun (.45-70 Government)
items.notes: Heavy mechanical multi-barrel machine gun operated via hand crank. Requires a static wheeled carriage or tripod mount.

items.name: MP5 Submachine Gun (9mm)
items.notes: Highly precise modern tactical submachine gun firing from a closed bolt; ubiquitous among global counter-terror forces.

items.name: Dynamite (Per Stick)
items.notes: Industrial blasting explosive compound. Highly volatile and prone to weeping nitroglycerin if exposed to excessive heat or prolonged age.

items.name: Browning Automatic Rifle M1918 (.30-06)
items.notes: Heavy selective-fire infantry weapon. Can be fired from the hip while walking, providing devastating suppressive fire.

items.name: Uzi Submachine Gun (9mm)
items.notes: Compact Israeli open-bolt SMG. Folds down for easy concealment under a heavy coat; high rate of fire burns through magazines rapidly.

items.name: M60 Machine Gun (7.62x51mm)
items.notes: Belt-fed general-purpose machine gun. Requires a team to move efficiently and set up, but can shred entire buildings.

items.name: Flamethrower (M2)
items.notes: Backpack-mounted fuel projector. Exceptional against biological horrors; however, a stray bullet to the tank turns the wielder into a fireball.

items.name: Bowie Knife
items.notes: Heavy fighting and survival blade, standard gear for wilderness expeditions and backwoods self-defense.

items.name: Large Club (Baseball Bat / Heavy Cane)
items.notes: Sturdy wooden or composite blunt weapon providing a reliable non-lethal self-defense option.

items.name: Pocket Knife (Penknife)
items.notes: Small utilitarian folding blade carried daily by most investigators. Minimal combat damage, high general tool utility.

items.name: Woodsman's Axe
items.notes: Heavy, two-handed felling tool that inflicts catastrophic deep-tissue slicing damage when swung forcefully.

items.name: Sword Cane
items.notes: A narrow, spring-released rapier concealed within an elegant walking stick. Snaps if subjected to heavy blunt trauma.

items.name: Brass Knuckles
items.notes: Concealable cast metal fist reinforcement; concentrates brawl impact force to crack bone easily.

items.name: Rapier / Small Sword
items.notes: Thin, thrust-oriented dueling blade. Requires specialized training to use effectively but excels at piercing deep vital organs.

items.name: Bullwhip
items.notes: Long plaited leather striking tool. Can entangle limbs or disarm opponents; capable of inflicting painful lacerations.

items.name: Garrote Wire
items.notes: Concealable length of piano wire with wooden grips. Lethal only from behind with a surprise attack on an unaware target.

items.name: Chainsaw
items.notes: Motorized logging tool. Inflicts catastrophic tearing damage but is extremely loud, heavy, and requires a pull-start action.

items.name: Taser / Stun Gun
items.notes: Electroshock weapon firing barbed darts. Inflicts no physical damage but paralyzes the target temporarily for easy restraint.

items.name: Bullseye Lantern
items.notes: Oil-burning lantern with a adjustable reflective shutter panel to focus illumination into a single directional beam.

items.name: Flashlight (Electric Torch)
items.notes: Battery-powered handheld focus lamp. Early models are prone to sudden contact flickering if shaken during a panic.

items.name: Camera (Heavy Tripod View / Box Type)
items.notes: Requires high-grade explosive flash powder and several seconds of completely static exposure. Captures physical proof perfectly.

items.name: Digital DSLR Camera
items.notes: High-speed modern optical body capable of extreme low-light sensor adjustments and instant file writing.

items.name: Smartphone
items.notes: Combines a cellular transceiver, camera, GPS map data, and flashlight. Prone to complete battery drain or signal failure around active gates.

items.name: Darkroom Chemical Development Kit
items.notes: Trays, specialized red safety lamps, and fixative solutions required to develop raw film sheets manually without overexposing them.

items.name: Handcuffs (Steel)
items.notes: Heavy iron or steel ratcheting locking wrist restraints used to capture cultists or secure an investigator losing total mental clarity.

items.name: Fingerprint Powder Kit
items.notes: Specialized dusting brush, fine soot carbon powder, and clear adhesive lifting sheets to identify human prints on smooth surfaces.

items.name: Binoculars (Prismatic)
items.notes: Dual eye lens magnification instrument essential for scoping out remote compounds, island shores, or dynamic ritual sites from safe cover.

items.name: Geiger Counter
items.notes: Detects ionizing radiation emissions. Useful for tracking meteoric impacts or bizarre residual anomalies left behind by Colour out of Space events.

items.name: Lockpick Set
items.notes: Tension wrenches and various pin rakes. Illegal to carry in some eras without a PI license; essential for bypassing stubborn doors.

items.name: 50ft Hemp Rope
items.notes: Thick, braided climbing cord. Crucial for descending into subterranean crypts or pulling heavy loads out of sinkholes.

items.name: Grappling Hook
items.notes: Multi-pronged metal anchor tied to a rope. Tossed to catch on upper-story ledges or secure climbing lines over slick walls.

items.name: Magnifying Glass
items.notes: Optical lens for examining trace evidence, forged documents, or tiny bloodstains invisible to the naked eye.

items.name: Compass
items.notes: Magnetic navigation instrument. Becomes wildly erratic or spins aimlessly when in close proximity to deep underground Mi-Go technology.

items.name: Chalk
items.notes: Simple marking tool. Essential for mapping twisting cave complexes or marking safe paths in labyrinthine dreamlands.

items.name: Box of Matches / Zippo Lighter
items.notes: Reliable flame source. Crucial for igniting torches, lanterns, or improvised incendiary devices.

items.name: Tape Recorder (Reel-to-Reel)
items.notes: Magnetic audio recording device. Heavy and somewhat fragile; perfect for capturing EVPs or logging interviews with fading witnesses.

items.name: Walkie-Talkies (Pair)
items.notes: Short-range radio transceivers. Allows teams to split up and coordinate without shouting, though batteries drain quickly in the cold.

items.name: Night Vision Goggles
items.notes: Infrared/optical amplification headset. Renders total darkness as a green-hued day, but ruins depth perception and relies on scarce batteries.

items.name: Doctor's Bag (Field Medical Kit)
items.notes: Fitted with scalpels, antiseptic alcohols, morphine vials, and sterile gauze. Essential to perform First Aid checks without penalty dice.

items.name: Laudanum Vials / Morphine Syrettes
items.notes: Potent opium derivative that dulls physical torment and pain, but does nothing to repair deep psychological or Sanity fractures.

items.name: Psychiatric Sedatives (Modern Anti-Psychotics)
items.notes: Advanced chemical prescription tablets designed to suppress short-term manic episodes or hysterical breaks during high-stress encounters.

items.name: Smelling Salts (Ammonia Inhalants)
items.notes: Pungent chemical capsule snapped under the nose to instantly rouse an investigator knocked unconscious by physical or concussive force.

items.name: Chemical Poison Antidote Kit
items.notes: Universal clinical charcoal pumps and broad-spectrum antitoxins to stabilize a victim of deliberate organic or exotic cult poisoning.

items.name: Straightjacket
items.notes: Heavy canvas restraint with long sleeves. The safest non-chemical method to contain an investigator undergoing a psychotic break or violent possession.

items.name: Adrenaline Injector (EpiPen)
items.notes: Auto-injector of epinephrine. Instantly reverses anaphylactic shock from exotic venoms or temporarily staves off fainting from blood loss.

items.name: Tourniquet
items.notes: Tight constricting band to stop massive arterial limb bleeding. Leaves the limb necrotic if left on too long, sometimes requiring amputation.

items.name: Translation Lexicon (Latin/Greek/Arabic)
items.notes: Academic linguistic references indispensable for breaking through ancient cipher dialects or ancient, coded journals.

items.name: UV / Blacklight Lamp
items.notes: Exposes deeply faded script variations, hidden fluid marks, or chemically bleached scroll edits on archaic historical documents.

items.name: Rare Mythos Book Facsimile
items.notes: A precision photographic or hand-copied bound version of a dangerous text. Protects original sheets but still offers minor Cthulhu Mythos skill growth.

items.name: Archival Storage Tube
items.notes: Air-tight, acid-free protective containment cylinder designed to stop dry papyrus maps or parchment sheets from shattering into ash during a rough march.

items.name: Ouija Board
items.notes: Parlor game turned spiritualist tool. Often opens brief, unintelligible contact with restless spirits, but occasionally acts as a beacon for worse things.

items.name: Spirit Box / EVP Recorder
items.notes: Rapidly sweeping radio receiver used by modern paranormal investigators. Captures fragmented voices or phrases from entities across the veil.

items.name: Crystal Ball
items.notes: Polished quartz sphere used for scrying. Requires immense concentration (and Sanity) to perceive distant locations or futures within its depths.

items.name: Embalming Kit
items.notes: Trocars, arterial tubes, and formaldehyde fluids. Used to preserve dissected corpses or sterile extract organs without rapid decay.

items.name: Horse & Carriage Rental (Daily)
items.notes: Standard urban public transit layout. Entirely quiet, but animals may panic wildly or bolt if they catch the scent of unnatural tracking entities.

items.name: Ford Model T (Automobile)
items.notes: The defining vehicle of the twenties. Loud, vibrating mechanical body that is incredibly simple to repair using standard Mechanical Repair skills.

items.name: Luxury Sedan (Cadillac V-16)
items.notes: High-powered, quiet, and fast heavy sedan chassis favored by affluent antiquarians and successful organized crime groups.

items.name: Four-Wheel Drive SUV (Expedition Grade)
items.notes: Rugged off-road vehicle with high ground clearance, winch fixtures, and ample trunk space for mapping gear, generators, and rations.

items.name: Motorcycle with Sidecar
items.notes: Allows agile passage through dense woodland clearings or coastal paths where full-sized motor vehicles are guaranteed to frame-lock.

items.name: Steamship Ticket (Transatlantic Class 1 Crossing)
items.notes: Luxury cabin travel crossing deep water paths. Gives the investigation group a solid week of uninterrupted study time before hitting land targets.

items.name: Commercial Airline Ticket (International)
items.notes: Ultra-fast flight passage. Saves crucial days of calendar tracking time when racing across the globe to stop a structural solar eclipse ritual.

items.name: Train Ticket (Coach Class)
items.notes: Standard long-distance rail passage. Crowded and noisy, but offers a reliable way to cross the country while avoiding roadside ambushes.

items.name: Bicycle
items.notes: Silent, human-powered transport. Useful for navigating narrow alleyways or dirt paths without the mechanical roar of an engine.

items.name: Rowboat
items.notes: Small, open wooden watercraft. Essential for reaching island ruins or navigating flooded subterranean caverns.

items.name: Biplane (Curtiss JN-4 Jenny)
items.notes: Wood and canvas early aircraft. Incredibly loud, freezing cold, and offers zero protection from projectiles or mid-air tentacle strikes.

items.name: Helicopter (Bell 206 JetRanger) Rental (Hourly)
items.notes: Allows rapid deployment to remote islands or sheer mountain plateaus completely inaccessible by road.
